rawFindings.title: IPv6 hosts are misclassified as having subdomains when the host header includes brackets
rawFindings.explanation: `req.subdomains` now treats any value recognized by `net.isIP()` as a single host, but `Host`/`X-Forwarded-Host` headers for IPv6 literals are commonly bracketed (for example `[::1]`). `isIP('[::1]')` returns 0, so the code falls back to splitting on dots and returns `['[::1]']` only by accident for some offsets, while `req.subdomains` on a bracketed IPv6 host with the default offset can still behave inconsistently with the intended 'no subdomains' behavior. A request with `Host: [2001:db8::1]`
rawFindings.suggestion: Normalize bracketed IPv6 literals before calling `isIP`, or strip brackets first and then return an empty subdomain array for any valid IP literal.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: A request with `Host: [2001:db8::1]` and default `subdomain offset` should produce `[]`, but `req.subdomains` can return a non-empty array based on dot splitting of the bracketed string.
